name: Dead-feed recovery gated on an unattended cadence hit
description: BP-INC-02 (card 68). Defining mechanism: the acceptance criterion is an event nobody triggered. A manual rebuild proves only that a human can write the file; the repair is proven only when the producer writes AGAIN, unattended, at its next natural cadence. The loop here therefore converges on an externally-caused observation and FAILS rather than emitting a partial when that observation never arrives - the opposite disposition from every other loop in this set. Environmental-versus-defect separation is delegated to live-estate-incident-triage as a subworkflow rather than re-implemented.

feed_name.description: The feed whose output is stale

producer.description: The scheduled task, daemon or job that is supposed to write the feed

output_path.description: The artifact whose freshness is the observable

expected_cadence_seconds.description: The producer's declared period. Staleness is measured against this, not against a feeling.

cadence_polls.description: How many cadence periods to wait for the unattended write before declaring the fix failed

add_freshness_postcondition.description: Leave behind a consumer-side freshness check so the NEXT staleness is self-reported

staleness-measurer.description: Measures observed staleness against the declared cadence, in seconds, from the artifact itself

producer-fixer.description: Repairs the producer or its freshness window, in the repo source and never in a deployed copy

cadence-watcher.description: Observes whether a write happened that nobody in this workflow caused

stages.title: Measure observed staleness against the DECLARED cadence

work_unit.title: Measure feed staleness in seconds against the declared cadence
work_unit.question_or_target: Record the output artifact's last write time, the current time, the observed interval in seconds and the ratio to expected_cadence_seconds; a feed is stale only when the ratio exceeds one, so 'looks old' is replaced by a number.
work_unit.evidence_requirement: last write time, reference time, interval in seconds and the cadence ratio - four numbers, so the verdict is arithmetic rather than impression
tests_required: a deliberately broken producer must make the ratio exceed one (the known-broken half of the control)
a healthy producer must keep the ratio at or below one (the known-good half)
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the cadence watcher re-reads the artifact's timestamp itself rather than this record
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:INC-6801 when all four numbers are recorded and the ratio is computed; otherwise FAILED:INC-6801 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to the producer's own log for its last successful write

stages.title: Delegate environmental-versus-defect to the triage blueprint
A power-off window is not a dead feed
Repair the producer or its freshness window, in the repo source

work_unit.title: Repair the producer in the repo source and record what changed
work_unit.question_or_target: Change the producer or its freshness window at its REPO source - never a deployed copy, which the next deploy overwrites - and record the diff plus the mechanism by which the change reaches the running schedule.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: a change to a scheduled producer is substantive

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the repo path changed, the diff, and the deploy mechanism that carries it to the live schedule - a deployed-copy edit is recorded as a defect of the fix, not as the fix
tests_required: an edit whose only target is a deployed copy must be rejected
the changed repo file must be shown to be the one the live schedule actually loads
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: an independent reviewer confirms the edited path is the source of truth, not a deploy target
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:INC-6802 when the repo-source change and its deploy path are recorded; otherwise FAILED:INC-6802 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to widening the freshness window instead of changing the producer

stages.title: Rebuild once by hand - explicitly NOT the proof
Wait for a write nobody in this workflow caused

body.title: One poll: has the producer written again on its own

work_unit.title: Observe whether the producer wrote again without any manual trigger
work_unit.question_or_target: Compare the artifact's current write time against the timestamp recorded for the manual rebuild and against this workflow's own action log; a write counts as UNATTENDED only when its timestamp is later than the manual rebuild AND no action in this workflow's log could have caused it.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the whole acceptance criterion rests on this observation

work_unit.evidence_requirement: two timestamps and a negative: the manual-rebuild time, the observed write time, and the absence of any workflow action between them that could have written the file
tests_required: a write caused by this workflow must NOT count as unattended (the attribution control)
killing the producer mid-flight must be recorded as forensically silent rather than as a clean absence of error
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: an independent reviewer checks the attribution negative, not just the timestamps
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:INC-6803 when an unattended write is observed with its attribution negative, or the poll records none; otherwise FAILED:INC-6803 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry inside a poll - the loop is the retry, bounded by cadence_polls

stages.title: The manual rebuild is not proof; only the unattended hit is
Leave behind a consumer-side freshness check so the next staleness self-reports

impact.blast_radius: changes one producer's source plus its freshness window; the wall-clock cost is dominated by WAITING for a cadence, not by compute

mechanism_fingerprint.not_a_duplicate_because: BP-INC-01 decides whether a disruptive action is justified and stops. This is the reactive repair of ONE feed whose only accepted proof is an event nobody triggered - the only loop in this set that FAILS rather than emitting a partial when its metric never moves.

worked_example.name: the recall index rebuilt itself hours later, which is what closed the incident
worked_example.narrative: Observed interval 373,680s against a 21,600s cadence, ratio 17.3 - stale by arithmetic. The triage subworkflow attributes 102.3 of the 103.8 stale hours to a measured power-off window but the residual 1.5 hours still exceeds one cadence, so the claim stays DEFECT. The freshness window in the producer's repo source is widened and a stale-input guard is fixed; a manual rebuild succeeds, and the workflow explicitly does NOT close on it. Poll 2, roughly six hours later, finds a write later than the manual rebuild with no workflow action in between - the unattended hit - and only then does the gate pass. A consumer-side freshness postcondition is left behind so the next staleness reports itself instead of waiting to be noticed.
